minimalSdkGap.existingPublicEntry: Original browser.proxy.managed status, enable and STOP operations
minimalSdkGap.failure: A sandbox cannot read Chrome proxy settings directly. The old status response lacked the verified active route and native mode needed to distinguish saved intent from actual state after reopening, or to confirm system fallback after owned STOP.
minimalSdkGap.whyToolOnlyCouldNotResolve: Persisting the selected route would misrepresent native state after pending edits, foreign changes, permission loss or unknown outcomes. Tool storage cannot certify exact PAC ownership or native mode.
minimalSdkGap.crossToolValue: Any independently installed consumer of the original managed-proxy SDK can show verified state after reopening without new privileged access.
minimalSdkGap.publicChange: Optional read-only browserMode and activeConfig fields on existing status output; no new write API or Driver replacement bypass.
minimalSdkGap.activeConfigBoundary: Return declarative configuration only for enabled, permission-valid, same-installation journal and exact PAC ownership with verified control. Unknown, foreign ownership, revoked or conflicting states return no active configuration.
minimalSdkGap.consumerBoundary: Match the verified declarative route to current user configuration exactly. Do not infer actual state from saved selection. Preflight replacement, owned STOP, confirmed-disabled status, concurrent configuration check and separately reviewed Enable remain sequential.
minimalSdkGap.security: Original capability, exact one-use Host review, global lock, installation identity, permission/revocation, PAC marker and unknown-outcome fences retained. No arbitrary PAC, authenticated route or general private endpoint approval added.
minimalSdkGap.systemSemantics: Clearing this extension's setting can expose another underlying setting. System success therefore requires native system readback; no unmarked explicit system override is installed. Chrome levelOfControl identifies extension control, not individual tool ownership.
